findings.evidence: `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE` is a read-only admin command (planner builds `*plannercore.AdminShowBDRRole`, executor reads meta only), but it is not included in the AdminStmt read-only whitelist: `pkg/parser/ast/util.go:58` (switch lists `AdminShowTelemetry/AdminShowDDL/...` but not `AdminShowBDRRole`). Read-only mode enforcement blocks statements not allowed/read-only: `pkg/planner/optimize.go:153` calls `allowInReadOnlyMode`, which falls back to `IsReadOnly(node, vars)` for non-`*ast.ShowStmt` etc (`pkg/planner/optimize.go:417`).
findings.fix: Include `AdminShowBDRRole` in the read-only AdminStmt cases (in this commit’s layout, add it to the whitelist in `pkg/parser/ast/util.go:58`). Alternatively, special-case `*ast.AdminStmt` read-only SHOW variants in `allowInReadOnlyMode`.
findings.impact: When `RestrictedReadOnly`/`TiDBSuperReadOnly` is enabled, `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE` will be rejected with `ErrSQLInReadOnlyMode` even though it performs no writes, blocking operators from querying cluster BDR role under read-only deployments.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master`: `git show upstream/master:pkg/parser/ast/util.go` still whitelists only `AdminShowDDL/AdminShowDDLJobs/AdminShowSlow/...` and still excludes `AdminShowBDRRole` (see snippet around `upstream/master:pkg/parser/ast/util.go` line 65 in the shown output). Read-only gating remains based on read-only classification (`git show upstream/master:pkg/planner/optimize.go` shows the same allow-list + read-only fallback).
findings.verify: Enable restricted/super read-only mode (e.g. set the corresponding global knobs) and execute `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE`; it should succeed and return 1 row. Also verify `ADMIN SET BDR ROLE ...` remains blocked without `RESTRICTED_REPLICA_WRITER_ADMIN` in read-only mode.
findings.what: `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE` is misclassified as non-read-only, so it is blocked in cluster read-only modes.

findings.evidence: `AdminShowBDRRoleExec.Next` mutates output (`req.AppendString`) and executor state (`e.done=true`) inside a retryable `kv.RunInNewTxn(..., true, ...)` closure: `pkg/executor/executor.go:2764`. `kv.RunInNewTxn` can re-run the closure after a successful `f` when commit hits retryable errors / the `mockCommitErrorInNewTxn` failpoint: `pkg/kv/txn.go:106` (loop + failpoint at `pkg/kv/txn.go:146` + retry path at `pkg/kv/txn.go:166`).
findings.fix: Make the `RunInNewTxn` closure side-effect-free w.r.t. result materialization: read `role` into a local variable inside the closure, return nil, then append to `req` and set `e.done` after `RunInNewTxn` returns success. (Or pass `retryable=false` if retries are unnecessary for this read-only path.)
findings.impact: If `RunInNewTxn` retries after the closure has appended once (e.g. commit retryable error or `mockCommitErrorInNewTxn=retry_once`), `req.AppendString` can run multiple times in a single `Next` call, yielding duplicate rows (or leaving `e.done=true` on an eventual error path), violating SQL result semantics.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master`: the executor moved to `pkg/executor/show_bdr_role.go` but still appends to `req` and sets `done` inside the `RunInNewTxn(..., true, ...)` closure (`git show upstream/master:pkg/executor/show_bdr_role.go`, see lines around 42–51 in the shown output). `RunInNewTxn` still retries closure+commit and still has `mockCommitErrorInNewTxn` failpoint (`git show upstream/master:pkg/kv/txn.go`).
findings.verify: With failpoints enabled, set `mockCommitErrorInNewTxn=retry_once` and run `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE`; it should still return exactly one row. Also validate behavior under injected retryable commit errors (no duplicated rows).
findings.what: `ADMIN SHOW BDR ROLE` executor is not retry-safe: it appends rows inside a retryable `RunInNewTxn` closure, risking duplicated output on internal txn retry.

subject: parser/executor: admin show/set bdr role (#48504)
summary: This commit adds `ADMIN SHOW/SET BDR ROLE` (parser grammar + AST, planner plan, executor read/write via meta). Two High-risk correctness/compat issues remain: the SHOW variant is not classified as read-only (blocked in read-only cluster mode), and its executor mutates result/state inside a retryable `kv.RunInNewTxn` closure (can duplicate rows on internal-txn retry). Neither is fixed on `upstream/master`.
